title: Linear-time universal simulation
statement: For every effective machine coding scheme $c$, there is a finite-tape machine $U$ over the Boolean alphabet such that for every Boolean code word $\alpha$ there is a natural number $C$ that works for every Boolean input $x$. If the machine decoded from $\alpha$ computes output $y$ on $x$ in exactly $t$ steps, then $U$ computes $y$ on $\langle\alpha,x\rangle$ in exactly $C(t+1)$ steps. Conversely, if $U$ computes an output $y$ on $\langle\alpha,x\rangle$ in some number of steps, then the machine decoded from $\alpha$ computes $y$ on $x$ in some number of steps.
hypotheses_covered: $c$ is an effective machine coding scheme
$C$ may depend on $c$ and $\alpha$ but works for every $x$
replaced:
Let $c$ be an effective machine-coding scheme. There is a finite-tape machine $U$ over
the Boolean alphabet such that, for every code string $\alpha$, there is a
natural-number constant $C$ for which the following hold for every input string $x$. If
the machine decoded from $\alpha$ halts on $x$ with output $y$ after exactly $t$ steps,
then $U$ halts on the pair encoding $\langle\alpha,x\rangle$ with output $y$ after
exactly $C(t+1)$ steps. Conversely, if $U$ halts on $\langle\alpha,x\rangle$ with output
$y$ after some number of steps, then the machine decoded from $\alpha$ halts on $x$ with
output $y$ after some number of steps.
